details: Bitcoin pared some losses to trade around $64,844, while Ether was at $1,814. Macro factors such as potential interest-rate hikes, higher real yields, geopolitical uncertainty, and cybersecurity concerns following the Binance hack are pressuring prices. Tech stock selloffs, including turmoil at Nvidia, are also contributing. Analysts anticipate Bitcoin to remain rangebound between $60,000 and $70,000 for the remainder of 2026.
title: Bitcoin Stuck Below $65K as Sentiment Stays Weak

details: Crypto engineering firm Temporal launched Supermassive, a fully on-chain perpetual futures exchange on Solana. The platform is designed to separate trading from clearing, enabling independent venues and market makers to compete for orders while a single shared clearinghouse backs positions. This structure aims to mirror Solana's spot market for derivatives, with a mainnet launch planned for January 2027.
title: Temporal Unveils Supermassive: Solana Perpetual Futures Exchange

details: The United States Supreme Court declined to hear an appeal from crypto-focused Custodia Bank, effectively ending its latest legal effort to gain direct access to the Federal Reserve's payment system. This decision means Custodia Bank will continue to rely on third-party financial institutions to process payments.
title: Custodia Bank Loses Supreme Court Bid for Direct Fed Access

details: US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) recorded a net inflow of $7.9 million on November 16, breaking a seven-day streak of outflows. BlackRock's IBIT led with $76.5 million in inflows. However, most other Bitcoin ETFs, including Grayscale's GBTC and Fidelity's FBTC, continued to experience outflows, and US spot Ether ETFs also saw net outflows of $8.4 million.
title: Bitcoin ETFs End Outflow Streak with Net Inflow
